characterization_methods.key_findings: For Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al, 24 h aging increases YS, UTS and hardness to ~2× as-homogenized levels and drastically reduces ductility (no numeric 450 °C/24 h value reported).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; averages of three measurements per material state

characterization_methods.key_findings: For Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al, hardness increases with aging; the 24 h aged state is reported qualitatively as ~2× the as-homogenized hardness.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: hardness (HBW) measured as part of RAP mechanical screening (Fig. 3d)
performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm

characterization_methods.key_findings: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in final materials; as-cast samples had coarse dendritic microstructure; hot rolling + water quenching gave fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 µm grain size and some retained Mn microsegregations.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: cross-sections perpendicular to the rolling direction; grinding and polishing with standard metallographic techniques

interfaces.phase_evolution: Aging promotes formation of nm-sized κ-carbides, producing pronounced strengthening with increasing aging time/temperature in the 8Al alloy.

phase_interfaces.coherence: lattice mismatch below 3% with respect to the austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix (cuboidal nanoprecipitates)

interfaces.slip_behavior: Orowan bypassing of longitudinal κ-carbide rods with subsequent expansion of dislocation loops, assisted by dislocation cross-slip; minor shearing of κ-carbides

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: YS, UTS, hardness (increase) and ductility/total elongation (reduction) relative to the as-homogenized state
comparative_performance.improvement_percentage: YS, UTS and hardness increased to levels twice as high (≈2×) as in the as-homogenized state; ductility drastically reduced

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five different alloys synthesized in one operation using five movable Cu molds filled successively from a 4-kg ingot; Al was charged through an air lock to adjust melt composition.
10 × 50 × 130 mm³-sized blocks were hot rolled into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500-mm-long sheets.
After this step, sheets were cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into sets of nine segments (2 × 60 × 55 mm³) for each alloy composition.
Scales were removed from surfaces by low-pressure fine-grit sandblasting after heat treatments; tensile and microstructure samples were prepared from the segments by package spark erosion.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All plotted values represent averages of three measurements for every material state; hardness measurements (HBW) were also conducted.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: tensile specimens prepared from segments by package spark erosion

precipitates.coherency: Lattice mismatch below 3% with respect to the austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix; forms cuboidal nanoprecipitates

microstructure_list.region: bulk (cross-sections prepared perpendicular to the rolling direction)

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized austenitic matrix (grain size ~20 µm) with some retained Mn microsegregations, containing nm-sized κ-carbide (L'1₂-type) precipitates formed during aging.

unmapped_findings: Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al is identified in the paper as the material with the highest Al content and lowest density among the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl (x = 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 wt.%) RAP series; no numeric density value is reported for this 8Al variant (b0024).

The specific aging condition 450 °C/24 h is not individually plotted in Fig. 3 (the colored aging conditions shown there include 450 °C/1 h but not 450 °C/24 h); therefore no numeric YS/UTS/TE/hardness values are reported in the text or figures for this exact sample (b0022, figure_003).

κ-carbides in the Fe-Mn-Al-C system have approximate stoichiometry (Fe,Mn)₃AlC and are thermally very stable at 600 °C, prevailing even after 100 h heat treatment with only modest coarsening (b0015, b0025).
